requirements.statement: Then a Coverage analysis section. The coverage conclusion cites the policy clause it rests on, and every exclusion that could apply is addressed and cited.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/## *Coverage analysis\s*\n([\s\S]*?)(?=\n## |$)/i); if (!m) return null; const body = m[1]; const hasClause = /clause\s+\d+(\.\d+)*|\bpolicy\b[^.]*\d/i.test(body) && /\[[^\]]*policy[^\]]*\]/i.test(body); const exclusions = [...body.matchAll(/exclusion\s+\d+(\.\d+)*/gi)]; const spans = []; const sents = body.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/).filter(s => /exclusion\s+\d/i.test(s)); for (const s of sents) { if (!/\[[^\]]*\]/.test(s)) { const idx = body.indexOf(s); spans.push({ start: idx, end: idx + s.length, why: 'exclusion addressed without a citation' }); } } const ok = hasClause && spans.length === 0; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'clause cited and every exclusion cited' : (!hasClause ? 'no policy clause cited' : spans.length + ' uncited exclusion(s)'), spans }; }
means: The Coverage analysis cites a policy clause and cites the policy for each exclusion addressed.

requirements.statement: Then a Decision section: covered or not covered, and under which clause.
End with a Reserve section. The reserve equals the sum of the invoices in the file, less any excess the schedule applies, and cites the invoices.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/^##\s*Reserve\s*$([\s\S]*)/m); if (!m) return null; const body = m[1]; const amounts = []; for (const mat of material) { const re = /(?:total|amount|subtotal|sum)[^\n]{0,40}?\$?\s?([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)/gi; let r; while ((r = re.exec(mat.text))) amounts.push(parseFloat(r[1].replace(/,/g,''))); } const invoiceMats = material.filter(x => /invoice/i.test(x.name)); if (!invoiceMats.length) return null; const sum = amounts.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0); const fig = body.match(/([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)\s*(?:dollars|\$)/i) || body.match(/\$\s?([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)/); if (!fig) return { ok: false, detail: 'no reserve figure in Reserve section', spans: [] }; const val = parseFloat(fig[1].replace(/,/g,'')); const cites = /\[[^\]]*invoice[^\]]*\]/i.test(body); const ok = Math.abs(val - sum) < 0.005 && cites; const start = text.indexOf(fig[0]); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'reserve matches invoice sum and cites invoices' : 'reserve ' + val + ' vs invoice sum ' + sum + (cites ? '' : ', no invoice citation'), spans: ok ? [] : [{ start: Math.max(0,start), end: Math.max(0,start)+fig[0].length, why: 'reserve does not match invoices' }] }; }
means: The Reserve figure equals the sum of the invoice amounts found in the material, and the Reserve section cites the invoices.

requirements.statement: Every figure in the work is one the request or the material gives.
I keep paragraphs to 5 sentences at most.
I hedge rarely: at most 2 hedging words per thousand.
The Summary section runs 25 to 33 words in my pieces.
The Facts section runs 47 to 65 words in my pieces.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
